developer_parking: Assumption about parking developers build without mandates: developers keep building the parking that renters, buyers and lenders want, so a repeal adds homes only where a minimum forced more parking than the market wanted. In Buffalo after its 2017 repeal, major projects provided 79% of the old minimum (mixed-use 47%; stand-alone apartments 117%). The scenario sets no parking ratio itself: it uses the permit outcomes of places that repealed, so whatever parking their developers chose is already built in.
north_carolina: North Carolina's HB 162, signed 6 July 2026, removes minimum parking for new projects statewide from 1 January 2027 (the 20 coastal counties are exempt). It is the closest real law to this scenario; it has no permit data yet.

places.evidence: Board of Supervisors passed the ordinance 7-4 on Dec 11, 2018; Mayor signed Dec 21, 2018; it removed all remaining minimums for all uses including residential (sources give effective Jan 20 or Jan 21, 2019). Primary ordinance PDF could not be read.

City project page says TC-11-21 removes minimum vehicle parking requirements wherever they apply and adds parking maximums and bike parking; council approved it 7-1 on March 15, 2022. Effective date not found.
City 2040 implementation page says council adopted the parking/loading/TDM overhaul on May 14, 2021, eliminating minimum off-street parking citywide; published ordinance in effect May 22, 2021.

Legistar record shows Ordinance O-113-2022 (PLN-ZOTA-22-00014), approved Oct 27, 2022, consolidating parking rules into Article 16 and eliminating minimum parking requirements. Current code text and effective date not checked.
City parking-study page says Ordinance 21-27, adopted Aug 18, 2021 and effective Oct 1, 2021, eliminated minimum parking regulations citywide; TDM applies to larger projects.

Secondary sources say the Green Code, adopted at end of 2016 and effective Jan 2017, has no minimum parking for any use, with a TDM plan required for larger projects. Rated near because large projects go through TDM review. City UDO PDF could not be downloaded; exact adoption date not confirmed (effective date is from PRN).

Planning and Zoning Commission minutes from June 30, 2025 show the petition to restore residential parking minimums under section 8.20.1 failed (4 votes, needed 5) and was denied. Original 2021 adoption is from PRN; current code text not read. Watch for later attempts.

News reports say the commission removed minimum parking for new development in 2022 (Ordinance 211262 per PRN), keeping maximums and a structured-parking rule for big lots. The single-family zoning repeal passed the same autumn and was reversed in 2023, which overlaps with the parking repeal. Municode text not read.

City approval notice says ORD-22-13, adopted Aug 15, 2022, eliminates minimum vehicle parking citywide and takes effect 10 days after publication on Aug 25, 2022 (effective date calculated from that).
Streetsblog reports the Planning & Zoning Commission voted unanimously on about Dec 12, 2017 to remove parking minimums citywide, after a 2016 first phase. No PRN citation; city code not read.
Petition (Ordinance 2022-5) sets minimum accessory parking at 0 spaces for all uses in all districts in section 6.36, including single-family and multifamily. Council approved it 8-1 on Oct 24, 2022.

The Nov-2021 amendment redline changes 'Minimum parking requirement applies' from Yes to No in every residential district (RA through RMF), and in other districts as well. Code history cites Ord. 42205 of 11-15-21. PRN gives Nov 1, 2021, but the code history points to Nov 15, 2021.

The ordinance replaces AMC 30-7 and says no off-street vehicle parking is required for any use, including residential. It was on the Nov 16, 2021 agenda for final passage and takes effect 30 days later, which matches PRN's Dec 16, 2021.

Special Ordinance 2022-28 repeals all parking mandates within city limits and directs the City Manager not to enforce them (passed 11/21/2022, effective 12/31/2022). Ord. 2023-19 then re-enacted LDC 4.1, saying a minimum number of off-street spaces is not required.

WAMC 19.44 sets only 'Motor Vehicle Parking Limits' (maximums) plus bicycle minimums, with history 'Adopted by Ord. O-2022-0024 on 5/3/2022'. The parking change came bundled with a full zoning code replacement.

Council unanimously adopted Ord. No. 22-10 on 12/13/2022, removing minimum parking citywide. Code 18.410 now lists vehicle maximums and bicycle minimums only. The effective date was reported as January 2023 (30 days later), but I did not confirm the exact date.

The council packet ordinance converts every Sec. 27-202 vehicle minimum to a maximum citywide. First reading was July 8, 2019 and second reading was on the July 22, 2019 agenda, but I did not see the final vote. PRN's 2019-01-01 looks like a placeholder.

Code 17.320.020 (Ord. 2022-008) says there is no minimum required parking for any use. Council voted 3-2 on Oct 24, 2022. The effective date is not confirmed (California ordinances usually take effect 30 days after adoption).

The city adopted a character-based zoning ordinance effective Feb 21, 2018, and the state's best-practice guide notes it has no motor-vehicle parking schedule (so no minimums). I could not open the code PDF that PRN cites (404).

Code 120-812C(2)(a) says no minimum number of parking spaces is required unless specified elsewhere in the chapter. The May 2018 staff memo lists 'minimum parking requirements eliminated' in the downtown-plan amendments, and the section history shows orders of 5-22-2018 and 6-12-2018.

The UDC (updated Aug 30, 2021) shows Table 6A converted to maximums and 6.3.3 amended. I could not find the ordinance number or date of the 2021 change, and leftover 'required' wording means a staff interpretation should be confirmed.

Code 9-4.404(f) says there is no minimum number of parking spaces for any use except accessible parking. July 2019 was only a Planning Commission study session; the Commission recommended the ordinance in Feb 2020, and it went to a council public hearing (ID-2020-102) in spring 2020 (likely April). PRN's 2019-07-19 is too early, and I did not confirm the exact adoption date. Event year set to 2020: the council heard the ordinance in spring 2020 (exact date unconfirmed).

Under Ord. 2018-0030 (4-10-2018) the former minimums became maximums in Table 94-87.1, and single-family types show 'None'. The 'shall be provided in accordance with' wording leaves some ambiguity for multifamily, so I rated it near rather than at pending staff confirmation.

B3 (adopted Nov 12 2019) made parking market driven with no minimums. The April 2025 B3 text and Ord. 2024-50 (adopted Jan 14 2025) now require one space per bedroom, so the repeal was reversed after about five years; the post-period must end before 2025.

Sec. 220-73 (amended by L.L. 3-2020, 11-16-2020) says there is no minimum number of spaces, but the Planning Board determines parking to meet realistic demand and larger projects must do a demand analysis. Discretionary case-by-case requirement rather than a pure by-right repeal.

Zoning ordinance (cover: adopted July 14 2020, effective July 29 2020) Sec. 6.3.2 says there are no minimum parking requirements except where specifically required; residential uses have maximums only. PRN date of Nov 4 2021 appears to be a later record date, not the adoption; municode was blocked so the 2020 adopted text was read from a 2022 mirror.

Site plan regulations list maximums with 0 minimums for commercial uses and leave unlisted uses to Planning Board discretion; the zoning ordinance has no general residential ratio but requires parking for ADUs. Could not confirm PRN's 2019-01-08 adoption date or what changed then.

Ordinance cover: adopted May 4 2021, effective May 21 2021 (city notice said May 12); Sec. 6.3.2 says there are no minimum parking requirements except where specifically required. City site PDF timed out; read via 2024 mirror.
Sec. 325-19B, amended by L.L. 2-2019 on 6-18-2019, removes any minimum number of accessory off-street spaces citywide. PRN date 2019-02-01 does not match the code note (2019-06-18).
Sec. 14.13.015 says parking is not to drive site planning, P3 parking is market driven and P5 has maximums; no minimum ratios. Adoption date taken from PRN, not confirmed in primary source.

studies.finding: 36 major projects provided 1,942 parking spaces against 2,444 under the old minimums (79%). Mixed-use projects built 47% of the old minimum; stand-alone apartment buildings built 117% of it.
studies.source: Hess and Rehler, Journal of the American Planning Association, 2021

studies.finding: Reported as about 18,000 fewer parking spaces over five years than the old rules required.
studies.source: Gabbe, Pierce and Clowers, Land Use Policy, 2020

studies.finding: Exempting old downtown buildings from parking helped convert them into thousands of homes.
studies.source: Manville, Journal of the American Planning Association, 2013

studies.finding: A financial model estimates about 12.5% more market-rate apartments; a model, not observed results.
studies.source: University of Denver with the Terner Center's housing simulator
